national_raw_news.title: Home Minister Amit Shah meets family members of anti-drugs activists in Punjab
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah met the family members of Vikramjit Singh in Batala, Gurdaspur, in Punjab, today. Vikramjit Singh was allegedly killed by drug traffickers recently. The Home Minister is on a day-long visit to Punjab to meet the family members of those who paid with their lives in Mansa, Gurdaspur and Sangrur recently for raising their voices against drug menace in the state. Mr Amit Shah will also meet the family members of Gulzar Singh in Sangrur, who committed suicide allegedly when his pleas were not heard by the state government against the sale of drugs, which made his son a drug addict. He will also visit Mansa, where an anti-drug activist, Parvinder Singh Jhota, was recently shot dead by a chemist for objecting to selling synthetic drugs. The Home Minister will meet his bereaved family members. The body of the activist has not been cremated by his family even after a week of his murder. Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, an ex-serviceman, while welcoming the visit, has demanded a CBI probe in the case. Meanwhile, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann has declared to hand over the murder case of Parvinder Singh to Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Later, Sh. Shah will participate in Dussehra ceremony at Ludhiana, where the burning of Ravana’s effigy has symbolically been themed as ‘Ravan of Chitta.’

national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) must convert the political vision of its leaders into practical cooperation that is visible in the lives of the people of the region. Addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Tajikistan today, Mr Singh said that the organisation’s 25-year journey provided an opportunity to review its achievements and discuss its future direction. The Minister emphasised that the three pillars of security, connectivity and opportunity are mutually reinforcing and essential for achieving tangible benefits for the people. Mr Singh said terrorism remains one of the gravest threats to peace and development of the region. He said that terrorism causes the loss of innocent lives, disrupts investment and economic capabilities, radicalises societies and deprives young people of opportunities. Mr Singh asserted that there can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in combating it, and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. He called for collectively dismantling the entire ecosystem of terrorism. The Minister said that India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new development opportunities. He said that the International North-South Transport Corridor and Chabahar Port could significantly contribute to connecting Central Asia with wider markets. Mr Singh stressed that connectivity projects must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries. Mr Singh also highlighted India’s experience in harnessing technology and innovation for development. He said India’s Digital Public Infrastructure has transformed public service delivery and expanded financial inclusion, while the country has built one of the world’s largest startup ecosystems. The Minister also said that India will host the first SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum later this year and invited all SCO member states to participate.

national_raw_news.title: Home Minister Amit Shah to Visit Punjab, Meet Families of Anti-Drug Activists Killed in the State 7 hours ago 137
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah will visit Punjab today to meet with the families of anti-drug activists who recently lost their lives after raising their voices against synthetic drug traffickers in the state. This includes the recent broad daylight murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was shot dead in broad daylight by a chemist selling synthetic drugs when Jhota publicly opposed him in Mansa recently. Our Jalandhar correspondent reports that the body of the activist has not been cremated by his family even after a week of his murder. His father has said he will not cremate his son till justice is delivered. Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, an ex-serviceman, while welcoming the visit, has demanded a CBI probe in the case. Meanwhile, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader and former Member of Parliament Harsimrat Kaur Badal, in a letter to the Union Home Minister, has requested to order an independent CBI probe into Jhota’s murder and the wider drug trade in the state. She has demanded an exemplary punishment for those responsible for silencing voices against drugs in Punjab. Mr Shah will also be meeting the family members of those who were allegedly killed in Gurdaspur by drug traffickers and the one, a father of a substance user, who committed suicide in Sangrur district. Later, the Home Minister is also scheduled to attend the Dussehra ceremonies in Ludhiana. Rajesh Bali/Jalandhar/Mail/0730

national_raw_news.title: Living Museum at Mizo Typical Village in Falkawn Draws Visitors, Promotes Mizo Culture and Traditions 3 hours ago 40
national_raw_news.content: The Living Museum at Zokhua, the Mizo Typical Village in Falkawn, is attracting considerable interest by offering visitors a chance to experience traditional Mizo customs and ways of life first-hand. Since opening, the museum has welcomed a steady stream of visitors. Set up by the Art and Culture Department, the Mizo Typical Village aims to give younger generations a practical insight into the lives and traditions of their ancestors. It also serves as an educational resource for schoolchildren, helping them better understand topics covered in their textbooks. Visitors can explore and buy locally made Mizo handicrafts, while the initiative also provides a source of income for local residents and young people. The Living Museum, which offers visitors a closer look at Mizo culture, holds live demonstrations every Saturday for an entry fee of Rs 100. These include demonstrations of traditional practices, along with cultural entertainment featuring folk music and dance. Officials of the Art and Culture Department said the initiative was introduced in response to the growing number of visitors from outside Mizoram and increasing interest in local tourism among residents. They said the museum was intended to offer visitors more opportunities to experience Mizo culture firsthand while helping preserve and promote traditional customs and practices. The museum has been attracting a large number of visitors, they added. Activities at the Living Museum include demonstrations of traditional village life, traditional dances, folk songs and dances, indigenous games, traditional Mizo cuisine and traditional costumes.

national_raw_news.title: 9 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Concludes In Mysuru Karnataka
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 9 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Concludes In Mysuru Karnataka Thousands Visit Mela Showcasing Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products of Artisans from 12 States/UTs Mela Featured 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans Hon’ble Minister Ramdas Athawale, Union Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam Mela Mysuru Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi The Nine Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 successfully concluded with thousands of people visiting Dasara Exhibition Grounds at Mysuru in Karnataka. The Mela was organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. The Mela aimed to provide a marketing platform for traditional handicraft and handloom products made by beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis, including artisans supported by the three National Corporations functioning under the Ministry, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC). Deputy General Manager in the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) Shri Rajnish Banker said the initiative sought to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for the target groups. He said the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022, and 975 artisans have been benefited through 13 such fairs organised so far. Shri Banker said the Mysuru edition was the first Shilp Samagam Mela of the financial year 2026–27. The Official said a total of 83 stalls had been put up at the Mela, out of which 80 were allotted to artisans, including 37 women artisans. Food stalls serving traditional delicacies had also been set up for visitors. The Mela featured artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, he added. The DGM informed that the exhibition showcased a wide range of traditional products, including handicraft items, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed products, Kanjivaram sarees, leather goods, wooden toys, bags and purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. The platform enables artisans to display their products to a wider audience and connect with prospective customers, while promoting India's diverse cultural heritage and traditional skills. The official further said that Shilp Samagam Mela also serves as a platform to disseminate information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and its three national corporations—NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC. The initiative seeks to enhance awareness about available assistance and development opportunities for eligible beneficiaries, while encouraging entrepreneurship and economic empowerment. The Ministry has also introduced BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) to expand market access for products made by the target groups through various digital platforms in India and abroad. Under this initiative, products are branded as BHARAT TULIP to enhance their visibility and facilitate online sales. The programme...

Addressing the 25th Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government in Dushanbe , Tajikistan , Singh underlined the importance of connectivity for shared prosperity. He said India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development. The Union Minister cited the International North-South Transport Corridor and Chabahar Port as initiatives that could contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets. “ Connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries,” Singh said, adding that projects not founded on these principles would not be sustainable. “Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment & commerce. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” Singh said. Recalling the deliberations at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in August-September 2026, Singh said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had underlined the need for concrete steps by the organisation on security, connectivity and opportunities. A greater number of institutions does not necessarily translate into greater achievements. New mechanisms should focus on clearly identified needs, avoid duplication, and prioritise delivering practical value to Member States,” he said. Singh called for consensus-driven action to address the uncertain global economic environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to trade and supply chains, concerns over energy and food security, and emerging technological divides. He stressed the need to strengthen resilient supply chains, facilitate trade and investment, and leverage technology to drive development. He also reaffirmed India's support for the adoption of an Action Plan for the Multilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation Programme for 2026-2030, emphasising that the benefits of economic cooperation must reach all sections of society. national_raw_news.title: Ponguleti announces revenue reforms to protect farmers' land rights - The Hans India
national_raw_news.content: Ponguleti announces revenue reforms to protect farmers’ land rights Home News State Telangana Hyderabad News Ponguleti announces revenue reforms to protect farmers’ land rights In Short Ponguleti alleges ‘negligence’ and ‘mismanagement’ weakened the revenue system under BRS government Venkateshwarlu Kolishetty Created On: 20 Oct 2026 5:15 AM IST Comment Share : X Revenue Housing, Information and Public Relations Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy chairing a review meeting with senior Revenue Department officials at the Secretariat on Monday A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Hyderabad: Revenue, Housing, and Information & Public Relations Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said the state government was restructuring the revenue system to ensure transparent public services, safeguard farmers’ legal land rights and provide permanent solutions to long-pending land disputes. He alleged that negligence, mismanagement and improper decisions during the previous decade had weakened the revenue system. Under Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s guidance, the present government was strengthening the department and making its services more accessible to the public. On Monday, Ponguleti chaired a review meeting with senior Revenue Department officials at the Secretariat. The meeting reviewed the implementation of the Bhu-Bharati Act, distribution of pattadar passbooks, statewide land resurvey operations and progress in resolving land disputes. He directed officials to improve field-level performance and deliver services transparently and promptly. The minister said the Bhu-Bharati Act, which came into force on April 14, 2025, aimed to create a Telangana free from land disputes. Since its implementation, 568,858 pattadar passbooks have been issued. Including 671,508 distributed earlier, the total stands at 1,240,366, or approximately 12.40 lakh. He said the resurvey programme was helping resolve decades-old disputes and identify farmers whose cultivation or ownership rights were missing from official records, preventing them from accessing government welfare schemes. In Narayanapuram revenue village of Kesamudram mandal in Mahabubabad district, a resurvey helped resolve land issues affecting tribal and non-tribal communities, granting formal land rights to 906 farmers across more than 1,600 acres. Similarly, a resurvey covering 15 villages in Nutanakal and Maddirala mandals of Suryapet district resulted in title deeds being issued to 2,400 farmers for 3,450 acres. Pattadar passbooks and title deeds will enable eligible farmers to access bank loans, Rythu Bharosa benefits and other government welfare schemes, he said. Resurvey operations are progressing in Mulakalapalli mandal of Mulugu district; Palwancha, Aswaraopeta and Dammapeta mandals of Bhadradri Kothagudem district; and Sathupally mandal of Khammam district. Ponguleti directed officials to extend similar surveys to other areas and ensure eligible landowners receive proper documentation. He stressed that government decisions would benefit the public only through effective field-level implementation. The meeting also discussed a proposed food park in Jangaon district. Revenue Department Secretary DS Lokesh Kumar, Inspector General of Stamps and Registration Rajiv Gandhi Hanumanthu, Jangaon District Collector Sandeep Kumar Jha and other officials attended. national_raw_news.content: India and Saudi Arabia discuss bilateral electrical interconnection initiative Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India and Saudi Arabia discuss bilateral electrical interconnection initiative ANI | Updated: Oct 20, 2026 03:50 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 20 (ANI): Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power, held a virtual bilateral meeting with Nasser Al-Qahtani, Assistant Minister of Energy for Electricity Affairs, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to review the progress of the India–Saudi Arabia Electrical Interconnection initiative and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation in the power sector. The discussions focused on the progress of the proposed electrical interconnection between India and Saudi Arabia, which holds significant potential to deepen bilateral energy cooperation. Both sides exchanged views on the way forward and underscored the importance of sustained engagement to advance the initiative. The two sides also explored opportunities to broaden cooperation in other areas of mutual interest in the power sector, with an emphasis on technical collaboration, knowledge sharing and the exchange of best practices. The Saudi Arabian side expressed interest in enhanced cooperation in the areas of Extra High Voltage (EHV) transmission systems, addressing technical and operational challenges associated with higher penetration of renewable energy in the grid, strategies for accommodating the growing power requirements of emerging data centres, and updating grid codes to address evolving power system requirements. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining constructive dialogue to further deepen the India–Saudi Arabia partnership in the power sector. On the other hand, India has advised its nationals residing in Saudi Arabia to exercise due precautions, move to the nearest safe place in the event of an aerial attack, and strictly refrain from filming, publishing or sharing any information, photos or videos regarding the ongoing events. "The Indian community in Saudi Arabia is advised to take due precautions under the prevailing situation. In case of an aerial attack, immediately proceed to the nearest safe place (inside a building or an interior room away from windows), and refrain from filming, publishing, or sharing any information, photos, or videos related to the ongoing events," the Indian Embassy posted on X. Embassy officials have continued visiting hospitals where Indian nationals are receiving medical care while remaining in constant communication with their families to provide necessary support. Flight operations remain suspended at Riyadh's international airport, while Dammam, Jeddah and Medina airports remain operational despite ongoing disruptions. Indian carriers have halted flight services to and from Saudi Arabia, with the Embassy outlining alternative travel options. "Indian carriers have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia, as outlined below: Air India, Air India Express, Indigo -- until Oct 24, on all routes. Akasa Air -- until Oct 27, on all routes," it posted on X. "Some available flight options are outlined below: Saudia: Scheduled flights to India from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina. Flynas: Dammam-Delhi and Dammam-Mumbai flights (Oct 17-24); scheduled Dammam-Lucknow services continue. Flyadeal: Dammam-Mumbai flights on Oct 17-18," it added.
